html:
The first empire-wide action against Christians, in 250, under the emperor Decius. He ordered every inhabitant to sacrifice to the Roman gods and for the emperor's welfare, before an official who gave out a signed certificate. Dozens of these certificates survive on papyrus from Egypt.

The order was meant as a show of loyalty to a new emperor in a time of crisis, but Christians could not obey it without denying their faith. Some refused and were killed, among them Pope Fabian. The theologian Origen was tortured and died a few years later. Many others sacrificed, bought certificates or hid.

The campaign ended when Decius died fighting the Goths in 251. It left a hard question: should those who gave in, the "lapsed", be let back into the church? Bishop Cyprian of Carthage argued for readmission after penance; the stricter Novatian split away. Later came the Great Persecution under Diocletian.
